newsitem.title: JAPAN: Panel may seek parliament role to choose BOJ chief.
newsitem.headline: Panel may seek parliament role to choose BOJ chief.

text.p: An advisory committee considering reforms of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) reforms is leaning towards requiring parliamentary approval for appointments of the central bank governor and deputy governor, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Tuesday.

"I got the impression that many members shared the view that parliamentary approval of the governor was needed," the official, who attended a meeting of a subcommittee of MOF's Financial System Research Council, told reporters.
They were unable to reach agreement, however, and left the issue for further discussion, he said.
The BOJ governor and deputy governor now require only cabinet approval.

There are currently seven members on the BOJ's policy-making board, including the BOJ governor. The four members who represent various industries all require parliamentary approval. The remaining two members are government officials with no voting rights.

The subcommittee members agreed that the number of board members should be expanded to nine from seven, including three from the BOJ and six from outside the BOJ. The three BOJ officials would include the BOJ governor and deputy governor.
The subcommittee is in the final stage of drafting a proposal on BOJ reform, based on a report issued previously by a study group under Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

Although the study group suggested some steps to curb the government's authority over the Bank of Japan, it fell short of recommending that the BOJ be given independence equal to that of central banks in other major nations.
Some politicians have recently criticised the subcommittee's deliberations for moving in the opposite direction of granting more independence to the central bank.

The subcommittee will meet again on Thursday to discuss thorny issues at the heart of enhancing BOJ independence, such as the extent of MOF's supervisory authority over the central bank and coordination between MOF and the central bank on formulating monetary policy.
The MOF official said the subcommittee will likely come up with a final report in early February.

At today's meeting, the subcommittee members endorsed the removal of the current ceiling on the amount of BOJ note issues and recommended the abolition of collateral requirements for such note issues.
